title: Spoken Word: Poems for the Stage

steps.prompt: Think of a song lyric or a line you can't get out of your head. Why does it stick?

cards.title: Spoken word
cards.body: Spoken word is poetry written to be performed. Listeners can't re-read a line, so poets use rhythm, repetition, pauses and their own voice to carry the poem. It often tells the truth about who the poet is.

cards.title: Rhythm and stress
cards.body: Every word has a strong beat: THUN-der, be-GIN. When strong beats fall in a pattern, a poem gets rhythm, like a drum. Read your lines to a steady beat and mark where the stresses land.

cards.title: A line that comes back
cards.text:
I come from loud kitchens,
from Sunday songs and burnt toast.
I come from stories
told twice and laughed at three times.
I come from here.
cards.note: “I come from” returns like a chorus. Each time, the audience knows where they are, and waits for what comes next.

cards.title: Feel the beat
cards.prompt: Tap the two words you'd say with the most force.
cards.text:
They said I was too quiet.
Listen now.

prompts: Which line did you choose to repeat, and why that one?
How did reading with the beat (or recording yourself) change your poem?
